title.narrative: Empowering Central Asian Youth for Sustainable Development and Inclusion

description.narrative:
The UNESCO Almaty Regional Office's 2024-2025 workplan aims to empower youth in Central Asia, focusing on Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, and Turkmenistan. Aligned with the UN Youth 2030 Strategy and UNESCO’s Operational Strategy on Youth (2014-2021), it addresses youth challenges like unemployment, education access, and climate change, heightened by the COVID-19 pandemic. The plan includes key initiatives such as the Youth As Researchers program, the Turaqty Jol campaign, the Global Youth Forum, and capacity-building for Civil Society Organizations.
Key outcomes include:
- Strengthened youth knowledge through research on mental health and social issues. - Youth-led environmental action through the Turaqty Jol campaign in Kazakhstan. - Global youth engagement via the Global Youth Forum. - Capacity-building for CSOs in Central Asia to enhance youth involvement in development programs.
The workplan contributes to Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) like Quality Education, Gender Equality, and Climate Action. It aims to create a sustainable, inclusive future for Central Asian youth by fostering resilience and social equity.
